plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Entire streets in Pretoria and Johannesburg dissolve into clouds of lavender-blue as thousands of trumpet-shaped blossoms open on bare branches. Fallen flowers carpet the pavements in violet, so the city seems tinted from above and below.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking in October and often lasting into November
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America, but Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of street trees. Local lore says that a flower landing on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum morifolium
plants.description: Japan's autumn garden favorite bursts into pom-poms, spiders and shaggy, many-petaled discs. Late-blooming varieties are grown to peak in mid-October, filling shrines, parks and festival displays with brilliant color.
plants.bloomingSeason: September through November, with late-blooming varieties peaking in mid-October
plants.location: Japan, in gardens, parks and shrine grounds nationwide
plants.funFact: The chrysanthemum is the emblem of the Japanese Imperial family, and the Chrysanthemum Throne is the name of the monarchy itself. Autumn chrysanthemum shows are a beloved tradition.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: Just as summer borders fade, bare stems rise from the soil carrying airy umbels of shimmering pink flowers with ruffled, recurved petals. They give sunny, well-drained autumn gardens a late burst of color.
plants.bloomingSeason: September to October in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens
plants.location: Gardens in the British Isles and similar mild temperate climates (native to South Africa)
plants.funFact: Bowden lilies flower best when their bulbs are crowded and the neck of the bulb is left exposed to the sun, which makes them unusually easy to grow.
